text: Every Monday, from eight to ten in the evening.
Split the sentence into tokens, keeping the position of every word and number.
Token features select learned vectors. Their sum gives each token thirty-two numbers. These are the actual values.
Learned filters mix nearby positions and neighboring words, giving each token local context.
Gates control how much context to carry forward. A backward pass adds context from the other direction.
Learned gates and hidden units combine token and sentence context, turning it into scores.
These are Monday's ten highest named role scores. Weekday wins. A separate score detects clause boundaries.
The scores become roles. The model does not calculate calendar dates.
Code combines the roles into a weekly window, then applies your reference date and timezone.
Eight P M stays fixed in New York, even when daylight saving changes the U T C time.
The API returns dates and calendar rules directly.
G P U time. A small neural model for everyday schedules.
